state.goal: Choose a PDF text extraction dependency for a controlled Python runtime
state.question: Which extractor can be installed and run in the production sandbox?
known_constraints: extract searchable text from unencrypted text PDFs within five seconds per document
deployment must comply with the sandbox installation policy
evidence: Scenario DEP baseline: the input is digitally generated text PDFs, without OCR, encryption, or advanced layout reconstruction.

Scenario DEP baseline: the authored fixture benchmark is 0.3 seconds per document with pdftotext and 4.0 seconds with pypdf; both meet the five-second budget, but pdftotext has lower billed CPU usage. The runtime allows pure Python packages.
Scenario DEP baseline: whether an external executable may be installed or invoked has not been confirmed; pdftotext is not preinstalled.
pypdf documentation describes a pure Python PDF library with text extraction: https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/stable/

alternatives.name: pypdf in process
alternatives.description: Install pypdf as a Python package and extract text in the Python process for the specified unencrypted PDFs.
advantages: fits the allowed Python package installation

alternatives.name: Poppler pdftotext subprocess
alternatives.description: Install the native Poppler pdftotext executable and invoke it as a subprocess from Python.
advantages: lower billed CPU usage in the fixture benchmark
disadvantages: requires an external native executable in the runtime
